## Claims
- [source-backed] The formal conjecture is that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal; \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6, lines 10-21]
- [source-backed] The two families are \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\). [source-6, lines 24-33]
- [source-backed] The paper reports computational verification for all bigrassmannians with \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\); this supports, but does not prove, the conjecture. [source-6, lines 46-54]
- [source-backed] The stronger suspected statement is \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\); it would imply the expected number of indecomposables and supports the minimality conjecture if proved. [source-6, lines 56-70]
- [source-backed] For \(n=4m\) and \(a=b=m\), the conjecture would give \(\binom{2m}{m}\sim4^m/\sqrt{\pi m}\) generators; this is a conditional consequence, not evidence for minimality. [source-6, lines 74-84]
- [source-backed] The separate open problem asks for minimal generating sets for general type-\(A\) ideals \(I_w\); it motivates the conjecture but neither proves nor refutes it. [source-6, lines 88-102]
- [computed] Prior exact finite certificates give \(J_v/A_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^2\) for \((r,n-r,i,j)=(2,6,1,1)\) and \((5,2,1,1)\), with both two-element prescribed families integral bases; these cases support the conjecture. [artifact 27afdb63404a159fb655ddde4867d0e60d06159e2e64e4f8523604222057256a]
- [computed] A prior finite Pieri computation for \((r,n-r,i,j)=(5,6,2,2)\), where \(a=3\), \(b=2\), and \(\binom{a+b}{a}=10\), reported quotient \(\mathbb Z^{10}\) with both prescribed ten-element families as bases; it is supporting evidence beyond the reported paper range, but lacks an independent implementation. [artifact 0b05e147fd3b8f028a0683ee0de19704b04f214954cc0d8c387547f8371d7299]
- [computed] The attempted independent elimination for \((5,6,2,2)\) produced \(431\) columns and \(2130\) Pieri rows but only \(420\), rather than \(421\), distinct complementary pivots for each family, leaving one unresolved nonfree column and \(109\) residual rows; the run exited with an assertion failure. This obstructs treating that run as independent corroboration, but is not a counterexample. [artifact 94a4a9e7aad3881f03af2eb14300f59d9ad3fbe215144562f8e6efcc61fc5fb8]

## Strategy
Use \(J_v/A_+J_v\) as the finite test object: an integral basis given by either prescribed family establishes irredundance via graded Nakayama. Retain only exact finite certificates; classify failed or non-independent computations as unresolved.

## Gaps
No counterexample is known from the supplied material. The \((5,6,2,2)\) supporting computation has not received successful independent reproduction. The general freeness statement remains conjectural.

## Next
Repair or replace the failed \((5,6,2,2)\) computation with an independently implemented LR/Smith calculation or a compact unimodular relation-lattice certificate.
